segments.source: To do this, set your split view controller’s [`primaryBackgroundStyle`](uisplitviewcontroller/primarybackgroundstyle.md) to [`UISplitViewController.BackgroundStyle.sidebar`](uisplitviewcontroller/backgroundstyle/sidebar.md), as shown in the following code.
segments.normalizedSource: To do this, set your split view controller’s [`primaryBackgroundStyle`](uisplitviewcontroller/primarybackgroundstyle.md) to [`UISplitViewController.BackgroundStyle.sidebar`](uisplitviewcontroller/backgroundstyle/sidebar.md), as shown in the following code.
segments.contextBefore: You can help your iPad app look more at home on Mac by applying Liquid Glass to the primary view controller’s background.
segments.contextAfter:
```swift
func application(_ application: UIApplication, didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any]?) -> Bool {

    let splitViewController = window!.rootViewController as! UISplitViewController
    let navigationController = splitViewController.viewControllers[splitViewController.viewControllers.count - 1] as! UINavigationController
    navigationController.topViewController!.navigationItem.leftBarButtonItem = splitViewController.displayModeButtonItem
    
    // Add a Liquid Glass background to the primary view controller.
    splitViewController.primaryBackgroundStyle = .sidebar
    
    splitViewController.delegate = self
    
    return true
}
```
